messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release r2026.03.15 -> canary-group 'frontend-v2' (10% traffic). Tracking healthchecks and 5xx ratio.

alice (oncall): getting automated alerts — healthcheck failures in canary. 5xx ratio jumped to ~7.8% on canaries, latency p50 doubled for some requests. Pagerduty page fired.

pagerduty: Incident P1 - canary-service: canary_health_check_failure (pager: alice)

alice (oncall): quick status: rolling deploy started ~T-6m. Noticed errors at ~T-3m. Service logs show repeated timeout to model-runtime /predict calls.

ben (infra): can you paste the metric windows and a sample log? I’ll check the router and the canary pool.

alice (oncall): metrics snapshot: `canary-5xx-rate: 7.8% (5m)`, `host-error-count: 42`, `avg-latency: 820ms (p50)`. Link: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/frontend-v2 (ops link). Sample error from canary-0: ``
2026-03-15T12:14:05Z ERROR request_id=abc123 downstream=runtime timeout after 30s waiting for kv-cache
2026-03-15T12:14:07Z ERROR request_id=def456 http 502 upstream:model-runtime
``

ops-bot: Detected quick spike in model-runtime latencies for sequence_length>2048. Canary abort criteria configured at 5% 5xx over 3m. Threshold breached.

carla (sre): we should trip the safety circuit and stop sending traffic to canaries. Please set abort flag and toggle the circuit-breaker. I’ll prepare rollback if abort doesn’t stabilize.

ben (infra): initiating abort now. Running: `./deployctl abort --target canary-group=frontend-v2 --reason "healthcheck spike 5xx"`

ben (infra): command output: ``
> abort request queued
> stopping traffic routing to canary-group frontend-v2
> re-routing test traffic to stable release
> abort applied (id=abort-2893004321)
``

alice (oncall): flipping feature flag to route all traffic back to stable: POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/toggle `{"flag":"frontend_canary","state":"off"}` -> 200 OK

ops-bot: Traffic shift completed. Canary traffic at 0%. Observed immediate drop in 5xx to 0.4% across fleet (5m window).

alice (oncall): customer impact assessment: short-lived errors for a subset of requests — we saw elevated 502/503 for synthetic tests and about 3 paying customers reported errors (acme-inc, beta-studios, walletco). Support notified. No data exfiltration.

carla (sre): starting automated rollback for deployment r2026.03.15 -> rolling back to r2026.03.14 on canary pool. Command: ``
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/frontend --to-revision=2026.03.14-canary
``

ben (infra): rollback in progress, watching pods. `kubectl get pods -l app=frontend --watch` shows new pods initializing and passing readiness.

alice (oncall): follow-up triage tasks: (1) collect runtime logs from model-hosts that timed out, (2) correlate requests with sequence_length>2048, (3) reproduce locally with stress harness. I’ve opened INCIDENT-2026-482 in tracker: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-482

carla (sre): hypothesis: change to kv-cache eviction / batching in runtime caused long tail for large sequences under light contention. Might be an interaction with new quantized kernels. Will reproduce in staging.

ben (infra): docs: added temporary mitigation note to deploy runbook and disabled auto-canary gating for this rollout channel.

alice (oncall): handing off to carla for overnight follow-up and RCA. Oncall swap at 00:00 UTC — carla will take lead. Leaving the channel. :white_check_mark:

carla (sre): acknowledged. I’ll own postmortem and customer comms draft. Assigning follow-ups to infra/model teams. Adding labels: canary-failure, rollback, customer-impact.

deploy-bot: Canary abort record created: abort-2893004321 by ben (infra). Rollback initiated.

alice (oncall): thanks team. Closing P1 once follow-up ticket has owners and customer messages are sent.

carla (sre): passing to night shift. Will ping if we see regression. :sleeping:
